title.narrative: Workshop on Climate Change and Sustainable Development

description.narrative: Despite efforts to promote sustainable development, Liberia remains highly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. The country’s long coastline and reliance on agriculture make it particularly susceptible to sea-level rise, storm surges, and changing rainfall patterns. These impacts pose significant challenges to the country’s development goals, including efforts to reduce poverty and promote economic growth. Moreover, it is proven that Liberia is facing numerous challenges related to climate change and sustainable development, including increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events, deforestation, and limited access to clean water and energy, there is a lack of widespread awareness and capacity at the community level to address these issues effectively. Communities often lack the knowledge, resources, and support needed to develop and implement climate-resilient strategies and sustainable development practices. Additionally, there may be a disconnection between national policies and local priorities, hindering coordinated action at the grassroots level. Consequently, there is an urgent need to empower communities with the tools, information, and skills necessary to adapt to climate change, mitigate its impacts, and promote sustainable development practices that enhance resilience and improve livelihoods across Liberia. To address some of these challenges, there is a need to build climate resilience and promote sustainable development at the community level. Community-based strategies can help to ensure that interventions are tailored to local needs and realities, while also empowering communities to take action to adapt to climate change and build resilience. However, there are significant barriers to implementing such strategies in Liberia, including limited resources, capacity gaps, and a lack of awareness and understanding of climate change issues among communities.
